topic: Chemical symbols derived from first letters
text:
Table 5.1: Elements and their chemical symbols derived from the first letter of their English names.
Boron: B.
Carbon: C.
Fluorine: F.
Hydrogen: H.
Iodine: I.
Nitrogen: N.
Oxygen: O.
Phosphorus: P.
Sulfur: S.
Vanadium: V.
Yttrium: Y.

Table 5.2: Elements and their two-letter chemical symbols derived from their English names.
Aluminium: Al.
Argon: Ar.
Beryllium: Be.
Calcium: Ca.
Chlorine: Cl.
Cobalt: Co.
Helium: He.
Lithium: Li.
Magnesium: Mg.
Manganese: Mn.
Neon: Ne.
Silicon: Si.

topic: Chemical symbols derived from Latin names
text:
Table 5.3: Elements with chemical symbols derived from their Latin names.
Antimony: Latin name Stibium; chemical symbol Sb.
Copper: Latin name Cuprum; chemical symbol Cu.
Gold: Latin name Aurum; chemical symbol Au.
Iron: Latin name Ferrum; chemical symbol Fe.
Lead: Latin name Plumbum; chemical symbol Pb.
Mercury: Latin name Hydrargyrum; chemical symbol Hg.
Potassium: Latin name Kalium; chemical symbol K.
Silver: Latin name Argentum; chemical symbol Ag.
Sodium: Latin name Natrium; chemical symbol Na.
Tin: Latin name Stannum; chemical symbol Sn.
Tungsten: Latin name Wolfram; chemical symbol W.
